children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE Futures canola contracts were stronger at midday Thursday, taking back Wednesday's losses as gains in the Chicago soy complex provided spillover support.
November canola was down by C$6.20 at C$832.90 per ton at midsession.
Continued strength in crude oil accounted for some spillover buying interest in the grains and oilseeds, as West Texas Intermediate climbed above US$100 per barrel.
Forecasts calling for the chance of frost in northern reaches of the Canadian Prairies over the weekend were also supportive.
The United States Department of Agriculture will release updated supply/demand estimates on Friday and positioning ahead of the data accounted for some of the activity in the North American markets.
An estimated 33,000 canola contracts traded as of 11:47 EDT.
